$description: Light mode theme — 12-step functional scales (Geist-style) + shadcn HSL semantics + Geist DS scale + elevation. Mirrors :root in @nebutra/tokens/styles.css.

8.$description: hovered border — DERIVED: OKLab lerp step5 → step9 at t=0.75.

1.$description: app tint — L* 99.01, C 0.003, hue 264. Radix blue-1 sits at L* 99.31 C 0.003.

5.$description: component background active — L* 87.77, C 0.052. Anchor for the derived border tier.

6.$description: subtle border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (deep scale, span 32.3 L*) at t=0.25. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 79.61, C 0.093.

7.$description: default border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (deep scale, span 32.3 L*) at t=0.50. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 71.63, C 0.134.

8.$description: hovered border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step9 (deep scale, span 32.3 L*) at t=0.75. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 63.47, C 0.175.

9.$description: solid fill — L* 55.50, C 0.215, hue 264.0. White label 4.99:1, inside the 4.7-5.4 band comparable products ship. Same value as shadcn --primary so the deep solid fill has one source, not two. The VI hex #0033FE (C 0.290, L* 48.4) stays the identity token --brand-primary and is deliberately NOT pinned into this ramp slot: pinning it left steps 6-9 only 3.5 L* apart with chroma climbing to 0.290.

10.$description: solid fill hover — L* 49.52, C 0.205. White label 6.45:1.

11.$description: secondary text — L* 42.04, C 0.180. 8.60:1 on step 1.

12.$description: primary text — L* 23.91, C 0.115. 16.38:1 on step 1.

contrast.$description: Label ink for the solid fill tier. Absolute value, identical in both modes: a deep fill always takes white, never the scale's own step 12, which is light in dark mode. 4.99:1 on step 9, 6.45:1 on step 10.

5.$description: component background active — L* 90.27, C 0.086. Anchor for the derived border tier.

6.$description: subtle border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step10 (bright scale: |L9-L5| = 4.9 L* < 6.0, so the tier continues toward step 10) at t=0.25. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 88.38, C 0.102.

7.$description: default border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step10 (bright scale: |L9-L5| = 4.9 L* < 6.0, so the tier continues toward step 10) at t=0.50. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 86.50, C 0.119.

8.$description: hovered border — DERIVED at build time (scripts/derive-border-tier.mjs): OKLab lerp of step 5 toward step10 (bright scale: |L9-L5| = 4.9 L* < 6.0, so the tier continues toward step 10) at t=0.75. The value here is a placeholder anchor only; the preprocessor overwrites it. Lands at L* 84.42, C 0.134.

9.$description: solid fill — bright scale, so the fill is LIGHT and takes dark ink: L* 85.41, C 0.164, hue 172.1. Ink 10.35:1 against --cyan-contrast. Step 9 legitimately sits above step 8 on a bright scale, exactly as Radix mint does (8 at L* 72.2, 9 at L* 87.0).

10.$description: solid fill hover — L* 82.61, C 0.150. 2.80 L* below step 9, matching Radix mint's own 2.95 L* step9-to-step10 drop, so hovering the bright fill deepens it slightly instead of collapsing past its own border tier. The previous value was 10.87 L* below step 9 and landed DARKER than step 8. Ink 9.40:1.

11.$description: secondary text — L* 51.64, C 0.100. 5.17:1 on step 1.

12.$description: primary text — L* 33.45, C 0.065. 11.35:1 on step 1.

contrast.$description: Label ink for the bright fill tier. Absolute near-black, identical in both modes, carrying a trace of the scale hue. A bright fill needs an explicit dark ink; comparing white against the scale's own step 12 picks white in dark mode, where step 12 is light, and measures 1.52:1. 10.35:1 on step 9, 9.40:1 on step 10.

background.$description: HSL channel triple — consume via hsl(var(--background))

primary.$description: Product action blue. Derived, not borrowed: hue 264 is the VI hue, L* and C were chosen inside the band the industry actually ships (measured OKLCH C 0.167-0.235, L* 54-67 across Vercel, Stripe, Linear, GitHub, Tailwind, Radix, Figma, Notion). #2e65ee = L*55.5 C0.215, white label 4.99:1. The previous 228 85% 56% (#2f56ee, C0.232) also passed at 5.70:1 — this trims it to the middle of the band rather than its top edge. The VI lock --blue-9 (#0033FE, C0.290) is 23% above anything in that band and must never surface on a component.

accent-foreground.$description: Softer brand blue — desaturated to match --primary, avoids 100% saturation glare on focus/accent

destructive-strong.$description: Red as FOREGROUND. In light mode --destructive already passes (5.42:1 on white), so this equals it; the token exists so consumers reference one name across themes. In DARK, --destructive is 0 63% 38% = 2.15:1 on --card, unreadable as text — see dark.json. Mirrors --warning-strong.

success-strong.$description: Green as FOREGROUND. --success (142 71% 29%) is 5.15:1 on white but only 4.49:1 as ink on its own 10% tint — one hundredth under AA, which is where badge green-subtle sat. Darkened two points: 5.71:1 on white, 4.99:1 on the tint, alongside --warning-strong (5.40) and --destructive-strong (5.42) so the three status foregrounds read with the same weight. Completes the trio; use --success for fills with --success-foreground on top.

warning-strong.$description: Amber as FOREGROUND on a light surface. --warning is a fill: at 38 92% 50% it is 2.04:1 against --neutral-2, so it is unreadable as text or as an icon stroke. This darkened step is 5.17:1, which sits between --success (4.92) and --destructive (5.19) so the three status colours read with the same weight. Use --warning for fills with --warning-foreground on top; use this for amber text and icons. Destructive and success need no equivalent — they already pass AA as foreground.

ring.$description: Focus ring — neutral foreground (Vercel/Linear/Cursor 2026 pattern). Brand blue is reserved for selected/active states; focus indication is chrome and stays neutral. Consumed by global :focus-visible outline as hsl(var(--ring) / 0.5).

ds.$description: Geist Design System color scale. sRGB hsla() fallbacks for legacy engines; oklch() overrides emitted via @supports wrapper for ds-gray-*.

ambient-sm.$description: Ambient elevation, small. Contact layer plus a wide soft pool — the marketing-surface counterpart to the tight xs..2xl product ramp.

ambient-md.$description: Ambient elevation, medium. Default resting depth for a floating marketing card.

ambient-lg.$description: Ambient elevation, large. One step up from md; use for hover of a md surface, not as a resting default.

glass-sm.$description: Ambient-sm plus a lit top edge, for translucent panels over a blurred backdrop.

glass-md.$description: Ambient-md plus a lit top edge.

glass-lg.$description: Ambient-lg plus a lit top edge.

sheen.$description: Top-edge sheen for solid inverted fills (bg-foreground). Lifts with light on a dark fill, with shade on a light one.

ambient-glow.$description: Centred offsetless halo — the only non-directional step on the ramp. For a translucent panel that needs separation from its backdrop without reading as lifted off a surface. In dark mode this inverts to a low-alpha light halo, because a black halo cannot read against a dark surround.

glow-accent.$description: Directional pool plus a wide brand-accent halo, for fixed dark-glass surfaces. The pool is theme-invariant black on purpose: the surfaces that carry an accent halo present the same dark glass in both themes, so a theme-flipping pool would lighten in light mode exactly where the panel needs the most separation. Accent sourced from --brand-accent, so it follows the light and dark accent values.

glow-accent-lg.$description: Hover escalation of glow-accent. Deeper pool, wider and stronger accent halo.

glow-accent-sm.$description: Accent halo alone, no pool. For a small accent-tinted chip or icon plate inside a glow-accent surface.

glow-primary.$description: xl geometry tinted with the action fill at 5 percent. For the emphasised card in a set (a highlighted plan) where the lift should read as coloured rather than neutral.
